case_name: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Special Leave Petition (Crl.) Nos. 7281-7282 of 2017
Sushila Aggarwal and Others ... Petitioners
versus
State (NCT of Delhi) and Another ... Respondents
Coram: Arun Mishra, Indira Banerjee, Vineet Saran, M.R. Shah and S. Ravindra Bhat, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 29 January, 2020

M.R. SHAH, J. and S. RAVINDRA BHAT, J. (Concurring):
1. The reference to this Constitution Bench was necessitated due to conflicting views on two vital questions concerning the scope of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973:
(1) Whether the protection granted to a person under Section 438 CrPC should be limited to a fixed period so as to enable the person to surrender before the trial court and seek regular bail;
(2) Whether the life of an anticipatory bail order ends at the time and stage when the accused is summoned by the court.

27. In Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 565, the Constitution Bench of this Court categorically held that Section 438 CrPC is a procedural provision guaranteeing personal liberty under Article 21. The Court in Sibbia firmly rejected the notion that anticipatory bail orders should be made for a limited time span as a matter of inflexible rule.

28. We are in respectful agreement with the ruling in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia. The judgments in Salauddin Abdulsamad Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra (1996) 1 SCC 667 and Mhetre (2011) which laid down restrictive rules contrary to Sibbia do not lay down the correct law.

92. Our final conclusions on the reference are as follows:
(1) The protection granted to a person under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure should not be invariably limited to a fixed period. In normal circumstances, the protection continues till the end of the trial.
(2) The life or duration of an anticipatory bail order does not automatically end or expire upon the filing of the charge-sheet or police report under Section 173(2) CrPC.
(3) However, depending upon the special features of a particular case or offences involving custodial interrogation or recovery of articles, the court may impose conditions or restrict the duration of anticipatory bail if warranted.
